steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
In large bowl mix flour and salt. Cut in shortening with two butter knives.
In a separate bowl, mix together egg, vinegar, and water. Drizzle wet mixture into dry mixture, cutting it in.
Roll out dough, and fit into two 9-inch pie pans.
Bake in the preheated oven for 12 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandma’s Secret Pie Crust
raw_recipe.description: The secret’s out! A great basic pie crust from Grandma’s secret recipes. Vinegar is the key to this dough that rolls out perfectly, and the bakes beautifully.
raw_recipe.name: Grandma’s Secret Pie Crust

review.reviewBody: I read all 100 plus reviews and the main thing I came up with was that chilling the dough for an hour helps. I also used a food processor to cut in the butter which I used instead of shortening. I didnt have to use as much liquid as stated. I added a little bit at a time. After chilling the dough still seemed quite soft and I thought it was goin to be hard to work with but it wasn't. My aunt (walking cookbook and great pastry maker) has tried for years to bring my pastry up from just passable and failed. After eating a quiche made with this my dad said I'll tell Aunty Ellen you've finally made it. Thanks

Perfect! I used all butter instead of shortening, chilled, and cut into the flour mixture. I also added 2 tsp. of sugar to the dough mixture for a little sweetness. I slowly added ice cold water, a little at a time, mixed into the dough until it came together nicely. The chilling of the dough really helped! After I chilled the dough, about an hour, I rolled it between two pieces of wax paper with no problems. The dough was soft and real easy to roll out-even for a beginner like myself. The results were a wonderfully-flaky and tender crust. The crust baked up nicely and formed a pretty light golden color. The crust tastes light and just absolutely delicious! It was simply a beautiful crust and I was impressed with myself. This will be one of those pie crust recipes I don’t want to lose! I used this crust for, “Perfect Pumpkin Pie,” also from this website. A perfect pie crust that I plan on using again and again!

If you have ever had trouble with pie crust this recipe is for you! I used butter flavored Crisco and had no trouble at all. I chilled the dough and rolled it between two pieced of wax paper and it came out beautifully. I would definitely use this recipe again and again!

I used the food processor instead and it came out well. When I add the liquid I did put the base in a bowl and didn't use all the liquid. Very flaky. I rolled it out between 2 sheets of wax paper and it was easy to put in the pie pan. I used half and will use the other half very soon.

I was a little irritated when I realized I had to make my pie crust by hand, as it's usually so quick to do in a food processor, but I'm in the middle of moving and it was packed. HOWEVER, this was so simple! And the results were amazing! I ran a little short on the shortening, so I subbed in lard for 1/3 of it. I've had this thing of lard in my pantry for far too long--my mom swore it made the best pie crust, but I don't make many pies... and now I was able to use it. Blabbering but Wow this was so easy, so flaky, so tender... I think I may have a new go-to recipe! Used as the pastry for Mrs. Siggs Pumpkin Pie. I am so proud of this pie!!--Update 1/30: Used crust recipe to make savory pop tarts (egg, bacon, cheese). Worked like a charm!

I doubled the recipe, used 1c chilled shortening, 1 1/2 c chilled butter. Also used apple cider vinegar because I don't have white. I needed an extra 4 T ice water, but my climate is very dry right now. Chilled the dough in the refrigerator before rolling it out, let it rest in my tins in the refrigerator after draping it in them. I made 2, double crust pies and had enough leftover for a single crust pie as well. Cut into strips for a lattice on one of the pies, the dough handled very well, didn't tear or break apart. The crust was flaky, flavorful and tender, everything I hoped for! The butter let it brown nicely, I did need to foil the rims halfway through.

This is the only recipe I've used over 15 years. I mix/knead everything by hand and the only adjustments are 1. if no unsalted butter or shortening are available, I just use salted butter and omit salt. 2. Reduce water to 3 tablespoons. Sometimes I don't use all the wet ingredients depending on how the dough feels as I knead along. Use the rest to brush the top. No need to chill, to prebake or anything. I bake at the bottom shelf and the whole chicken pot pie or apple pie come out crisp/flaky and buttery good.

I think this might now be my go to pie crust recipe. It came out flaky and soft, the last recipe I had gave me a fifty percent chance that it would be good and the other fifty percent was that it would be hard as a rock. I would definitely make this again. A few changes that I added to this recipe is that I added two extra tablespoons of water, rolled it out immediately after I made it, and I baked it for ten minuets before I put my filling in. I have to say it was one of the best pumpkin pies I have ever made.

Amazing! The best crust I have ever made, or tasted for that matter. Read all the reviews and followed the tips. I only swapped out 1/4 c. of shortening for butter for extra taste. In my case even after taking it out of the frig to roll out it was very crumbly but it came together once I dusted with more flour. I used it for the bottom and top of my home made chicken pot pie. The crust definitely made the recipe. Save this one to my recipe box.
I used 1 cup of lard and 1/4 cup butter for the shortening. Best pie crust ever. Put the crust in the fridge while I prepared my apples.

That's a keeper! I tried the recipe yesterday and I was very pleased. I didn't have shortening on hand and used 1 cup frozen butter instead of 1 1/4 C. shortening, but that was the only change I made. I has a nice buttery flavor and flaky consistency. I cut the frozen butter into chunks and used the food processor. Then I split the dough and chilled it for 3 hours. It was easy and velvety smooth to roll out. I did not prebake it and I will definetly use it again. Thank you very much.

This is a great crust! This recipe calls for more shortening (or butter, in my case) than the average crust and that, I believe, makes all the difference. Easy to roll without cracks and flaky after baking. I'm forever on the hunt for a better crust recipe and this just might be the best I've ever found. Very similar to my regular go-to recipe but with more butter. I'm sold and will definitely be making more of this. Thanks for this winner of a recipe.

This rolled out perfectly, it was so nice and moist and easy on the rolling pin. I did have to add just a couple more drops of water to make it a bit more pliable, but it was so nice and moist. It looked a little off once I baked it for the 12 required minutes, but I was more at-ease when I started to bake the actual pie. I was scared for a moment- it was crumbling a bit at the edges when I took my pie out of the oven. When we finally cut into it, the crust was so nice and light and buttery! Definitely will be using this for my pies in the future. I would just cover the edges of the crust with a bit of foil so as it doesn't burn, it seems to burn easier than other crusts.

I used this recipe for chicken pot pie and the crust was fantastic. Flakey and so good. I only use shortening, not lard or butter. I start by cutting in with two knives but also use my hands to get a consistency of small peas. I usually use more water than called for as I prefer working with soft dough. I also use an egg wash. Even after I freeze the pies, the crust is flakey
Simple easy crust. I like to use it for chicken pot pie.
I have been searching for years for a good pie crust recipe. This is the best!

I made this crust just as directed and it came out perfect! I used Crisco just because it was easier to work with than the refrigerated butter. I also didn't read the tips and did not chill the dough before rolling out. Mine came out great without chilling but I can see where it might help keep it more firm while rolling. Great recipe.

This is my favorite pie crust recipe. It comes out perfect each time. I make little cinnamon pinwheel roll ups with leftover dough. They are a big hit with my family and grandkids. I agree with previous comments it’s important not to over add the liquid, not to overwork the dough, and to let it chill in the refrigerator for a bit, 30 minutes at least. Then let the dough come to room temperature and roll it out.
